## Senolytics as a Treatment for Diabetic Kidney Disease  
[Permalink (With Comments)](https://www.fightaging.org/archives/2026/01/senolytics-as-a-treatment-for-diabetic-kidney-disease/)  
[Permalink (No Comments)](https://www.fightaging.org/archives/2026/01/senolytics-as-a-treatment-for-diabetic-kidney-disease/?nc)Posted by Reason  
[Type 2 diabetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_2_diabetes) is largely a self-inflicted problem, a consequence of becoming overweight. Aging makes it easier to reach the threshold needed for a diagnosis of diabetes, but the condition remains in principle avoidable for the majority of people, were they making better choices about diet and exercise. In recent years, researchers have linked an increased burden of [cellular senescence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_senescence) to the pathology of type 2 diabetes; the aberrant diabetic metabolism [encourages more cellular senescence](https://www.fightaging.org/archives/2025/06/type-2-diabetes-is-associated-with-a-greater-burden-of-cellular-senescence/), and the presence of lingering senescent cells is in turn inflammatory and disruptive to tissue function.
In today's open access paper, researchers focus on cellular senescence in [diabetic kidney disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diabetic_nephropathy). In this context the increased burden of senescent cells actively sabotages the function of the kidney. Thus [senolytic therapies](https://www.fightaging.org/archives/2017/09/senolytic-therapies-to-clear-senescent-cells-will-transform-the-field-of-medicine-for-age-related-conditions/) capable of selectively destroying some fraction of senescent cells can produce measurable improvements in kidney function following a single course of treatment. Given time, and no correction of the lifestyle and physiology that drives diabetes, senescent cells and kidney dysfunction will reemerge, of course. But senolytic drugs nonetheless offer the prospect of meaningfully reducing some of the harms done by aging and obesity.
